## Section 1 - Hero (`#top`)

**On-screen layout:** Two-column hero. Left: kicker + title + blurb + links. Right: giant “451×” metric.

- Kicker: STANFORD UNIVERSITY · SUMMER SESSION 2026 · INTRODUCTION TO HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTING AND AI SYSTEMS (ME344)
- Title: AlphaFold / TPU Benchmark
- Body: “We timed AlphaFold 2’s real JAX forward pass on Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU (2 vCPU), Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4, and Stanford GKE TPU v5e-8 (2×4 lite podslice). As a follow-up we also ran AlphaFold 3 on the same Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU (2 vCPU) and Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4; its public release has no TPU. Steady-state AF2 on Stanford GKE TPU v5e-8 is 451× faster than Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU (0.47s vs 212.1s).”
- Links: AF2 results · AF3 · Slides PDF · Reproduce
- Metric label: AF2 STEADY-STATE PREDICT VS GOOGLE COLAB INTEL XEON CPU (2 VCPU)
- Metric: **451×** (teal ×)
- Subline: 2nd predict · model_3 · 118 residues: Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU (2 vCPU) 212.1s · Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4 13.1s (16.2× vs Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU) · Stanford GKE TPU v5e-8 (tpu-v5-lite-podslice, 2×4, 8 chips) 0.47s (451× vs Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU)
- Footer credit line under a hairline rule: Lorenzo Pazienza & Ihab El Bani · Stanford University · Summer Session 2026 · Introduction to High Performance Computing and AI Systems (ME344) · Profs. Steve Jones & Mourad Bouache

**Important:** GPU speedup vs CPU is **16.2×**. TPU vs GPU is ~27.8×. Do not say GPU is 27.8× vs CPU.

## Section 2 - Structure (`#structure`)

**Headline:** Human ubiquitin  
**Supporting:** ESMFold prediction · 76 residues · mean pLDDT **90.5**. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom. Colors follow AlphaFold’s pLDDT scale.

### Media A - Interactive 3D viewer
- Asset (fallback still): https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/figures/ubiquitin_structure.png
- PDB: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/structure/ubiquitin_predicted.pdb
- **What it shows:** Cartoon ribbon of human ubiquitin. Residues colored by pLDDT confidence:
  - >90 deep blue (very high)
  - 70–90 cyan (high)
  - 50–70 yellow (medium)
  - <50 orange (low)
- Most of the fold is blue/cyan (high confidence). The flexible C-terminal conjugating tail (roughly residues 71–76) is warmer / lower confidence.
- Caption note: “Lower confidence at the C-terminus (residues ~71–76)”

### Media B - Per-residue pLDDT line chart
- Also available as still: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/figures/ubiquitin_confidence.png
- **What it shows:** Line chart, X = residue 1–76, Y = pLDDT ~40–100. Teal line stays high (~90–96) through the core, with a shaded band highlighting residues 70–76 where confidence drops (toward ~50s–70s at the end).
- Caption: “Shaded band: residues 70–76”
- Chart title on page: “Per-residue pLDDT” · mean 90.5

**Scope note (stated on site):** This ubiquitin fold is **biology / ESMFold with trained weights**. It is **not** the timed CPU/GPU/TPU systems workload (that uses Haiku random init on a 118-residue systems input).

---

## Section 3 - Problem (`#problem`)

- Kicker: Problem
- Headline: “Where does AlphaFold 2 spend time on CPU, GPU, and TPU?”
- Body: The problem - AlphaFold 1 showed deep learning could help; AlphaFold 2 (DeepMind) made high-accuracy structure prediction practical with a large JAX/Haiku Evoformer, but inference is still costly/opaque across accelerators. What we did - same AF2 forward pass (118 residues, model_3, 0 recycles, Haiku random-init) on Google Colab Intel Xeon (2 vCPU), Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4, and Stanford GKE TPU v5e-8 (tpu-v5-lite-podslice, 2×4, 8 chips); timed init, cold predict, steady-state; fixed bottlenecks.

---

## Section 4 - Approach (`#approach`)

- Kicker: Approach
- Headline: “One script, three backends”
- Body: Every timing run calls `spike_tpu_forward_pass.py`. Only the accelerator changes.

**Architecture strip (4 cells):**
1. Script - `spike_tpu_forward_pass.py` (AF2 `model_3`, 0 recycles, 118 residues)
2. CPU - Google Colab Intel Xeon · 2 vCPU → `result_cpu.json`
3. GPU - Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4 → `result_gpu-t4.json`
4. TPU - Stanford GKE v5e-8 · 2×4 lite (`tpu-v5-lite-podslice`) → `result_tpu + traces`

**Parameters note:** Systems timings use Haiku random init to exercise the same compiled graph without downloading trained weights (~350MB). Ubiquitin above is separate (ESMFold).

---

## Section 5 - Results (`#results`)

- Kicker: Results
- Headline: “Steady-state predict latency”
- Big callout: **0.47s**
- Subcopy: model_3, 0 recycles, 118-residue input, Haiku random-init. Backends: Google Colab Intel Xeon (2 vCPU), Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4, Stanford GKE TPU v5e-8 (2×4 lite). Identical code path; bar lengths are log-scaled.

**Latency bars (log-scaled widths on page):**
| Backend | Display time | Speedup vs CPU | Bar color (approx) |
|---------|--------------|----------------|--------------------|
| CPU Xeon (Google Colab, 2 vCPU) | 212.1s | 1× | gray |
| GPU Tesla T4 (Google Colab) | 13.1s | 16.2× | blue |
| TPU v5e-8 (Stanford GKE, 2×4) | 0.47s | 451× | teal |

**First predict / steady-state (compile visibility):**
| Backend | Ratio | Note |
|---------|-------|------|
| CPU Xeon | 1.28× | Mostly compute |
| GPU Tesla T4 | 7.46× | Compile is visible |
| TPU v5e-8 | 59.1× | Cold path is compile |

---

## Section 6 - Experiments (`#experiments`)

- Kicker: Experiments
- Headline: “Twelve TPU follow-ups”
- UX note on page: Click + on a row for method notes. Shared figures sit under each phase. Amber rail = negative result.

### Phase: Scaling

#### 01 Sequence length - **14.6×** (time for 8.3× length)
- Finding: Steady-state time grew faster than sequence length (8.3× length → 14.6× time).
- Notes: Swept 60, 120, 250, 500 residues. Super-linear; matches pair representation. Compile ~flat.

#### 02 Recycle depth - **~0.46s** (per extra recycle)
- Finding: Steady-state rose linearly with recycles; compile did not.
- Notes: 0/1/3 recycles; ~0.46s each added recycle. Compile jumps 0→1 then flat 1→3.

#### 03 Chip visibility - **1 of 8** (chips used)
- Finding: 1 visible chip and 8 visible chips gave the same single-query time.
- Notes: Default path one query on one chip. 2-/4-chip libtpu flag attempts failed.

### Media C - Shared scaling charts
- URL: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/figures/scaling_charts.png
- Caption: “Left: sequence length. Right: recycle depth. Same TPU v5e-8 runs.”
- **What it shows:** Two side-by-side line charts for TPU v5e-8. Left: latency vs sequence length; right: latency vs recycle depth (118 residues). Each panel plots orange “compile + run (1st call)” and blue “steady-state (2nd call)”. Orange sits much higher; blue rises with length/recycles more gently.

### Phase: Bottleneck & fix

#### 04 Profiler trace - **76%** (of first call in cache_miss)
- Finding: cache_miss in JAX pjit accounted for ~76% of the first predict call.
- Notes: `$pjit.py:250` ~12.55s self-time inside 16.56s first predict; TPU device nearly idle → host-side JIT.

#### 05 Compilation cache - **6.8×** (faster init_params)
- Finding: Persisting JAX compile cache across process restart cut init_params by 6.8×.
- Notes: First predict also ~1.9× with warm cache; steady-state unchanged.

#### 06 Precision (bf16) - **−40%** (steady-state HBM)
- Finding: bfloat16 cut steady-state HBM ~40% with little runtime change at this size.
- Notes: Wall-clock barely moved; peak memory briefly higher during cast.

### Phase: Multi-chip

#### 07 Multi-query batching - **lower** (proteins/sec vs batch=1) · NEGATIVE
- Finding: jax.vmap reduced proteins/sec as batch size grew; only TPU_0 used HBM.
- Notes: Batches 1/2/4/8; throughput never beat batch=1; memory stayed on one chip.

### Media D - Batching chart
- URL: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/figures/batching_chart.png
- Caption: “Wall-clock scales ~linearly; per-protein cost rises with batch size.”
- **What it shows:** Chart of batching experiment outcomes: as batch size increases, wall-clock grows roughly linearly and per-protein efficiency worsens versus batch=1; reinforces that vmap did not spread work across the 8-chip slice.

#### 08 pmap parallelism - **6.92×** (throughput speedup)
- Finding: jax.pmap ran 8 proteins on 8 chips at 6.92× single-chip throughput.
- Notes: 2.13 → 14.72 proteins/sec; per-chip HBM 445–469 MB ≈ single-protein footprint.

#### 09 Auto-sharding (GSPMD) - **0×** (tensor split) · NEGATIVE
- Finding: GSPMD auto-mesh left a full ~463 MB copy on every chip (no split).
- Notes: Root cause - AlphaFold ensembling is a sequential hk.while_loop; nothing for GSPMD to distribute. Reproduced twice.

#### 10 Real single-query sharding - **8/8** (chips genuinely used)
- Finding: Re-implemented AlphaFold’s ensemble average with pmap + cross-device pmean; verified correct on all 8 chips.
- Notes: AlphaFold source untouched. Steady-state 0.54s. Per-chip HBM 427–624 MB (not flat 463 MB replication). Scope: distributed ensembling, not full Evoformer tensor sharding.

### Phase: Fit & rigor

#### 11 Empirical scaling law - **R² 0.981** (16-point TPU grid)
- Finding: Power law on 16 TPU runs (4 chip counts × 4 lengths) fits R² 0.981.
- Equation: throughput ≈ 4527.77 · chips^0.963 · length^−1.572
- Implication: chip exponent near 1 → pmap scaling holds; cost/prediction nearly flat in chips.

### Media E - Scaling law chart
- URL: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/figures/scaling_law_chart.png
- Caption: “Throughput vs chips and sequence length on the measured grid.”
- **What it shows:** Visualization of the 16-run grid / fit: throughput rising with chip count and falling with sequence length, consistent with the fitted power law (R² 0.981).

#### 12 Model pick & repeats - **<1%** (stdev on repeats)
- Finding: model_5 ~15% faster at steady-state; three repeats stayed under 1% stdev.
- Notes: model_5 beat model_3 and model_4 by ~15%; all tracked metrics <1% stdev across three repeats.

---

## Section 6b - AlphaFold 3 (`#af3`)

- Kicker: Side investigation
- Headline: “AlphaFold 3 on the same backends”
- Body: Separate DeepMind codebase (Pairformer + diffusion - not an AF2 version bump). Same 118-residue toy input, seed=1. Trained weights ~1.15 GB. Five diffusion samples per call.

### Latency compare (per sample, identical Google Colab)
| Backend | AF2 | AF3 | AF3 / AF2 |
|---------|-----|-----|-----------|
| CPU (Google Colab) | 212.1s | 490.8s | 2.3× |
| GPU T4 (Google Colab) | 13.1s | 22.8s | 1.74× |

AF3 also gains more from GPU: CPU→GPU **21.5×** vs AF2’s **16.2×**.

### Media F - Interactive AF3 3D viewer + confidence chart
- Same component pattern as ubiquitin (`ProteinViewer` + 3Dmol.js).
- CIF: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/structure/af3_toy_test_cpu-colab_model.cif
- Fallback still: https://alphafold-tpu.vercel.app/figures/af3_toy_test_structure.png
- On-page kicker: “AlphaFold 3 · structure”
- Title: “AF3 toy structure”
- Subtitle: Diffusion sample, seed 1 · 118 residues, no MSA · **ptm 0.23**
- **What the 3D shows:** Cartoon ribbon colored by per-atom confidence (CIF `B_iso_or_equiv`, same pLDDT color scale as ubiquitin). Expect mostly orange/yellow (low–medium), not blue - correct for this input.
- **What the chart shows:** Per-residue CA confidence for residues 1–118; values roughly ~23–61 (mean CA ~43). No shaded C-term band (unlike ubiquitin).
- Caption (stated on site): “Low confidence throughout - expected for a no-MSA input, not a defect. Not comparable to the ubiquitin mean pLDDT above.”
- **Cross-model quality note:** Do **not** treat AF3 ptm 0.23 / low CA confidence vs ubiquitin mean pLDDT 90.5 as a head-to-head model-quality ranking. The AF3 toy run deliberately has no MSA.

### TPU wall (negative result)
- Every infrastructure step worked (native build, CCD, weights, `jax[tpu]` on Stanford v5e-8 Job).
- Inference died at flag validation: public AF3 `--jax_backend` only accepts `cpu | gpu | mps`.
- Log: `FATAL Flags parsing error: flag --jax_backend=tpu: value should be one of <cpu|gpu|mps>`
- Matches DeepMind docs (NVIDIA GPU ≥7.0 or CPU). Not an infra miss on our side.

## Section 7 - Cost (`#cost`)

- Kicker: Cost
- Headline: “Cost per prediction is nearly flat in chip count”
- Body: Choose chips for latency or throughput; do not expect lower unit cost from a larger slice.

**Formula block:**
- Label: Empirical fit · 16 TPU runs · R² 0.981
- throughput ≈ 4527.77 · chips^0.963 · length^−1.572
- Grid: chips {1,2,4,8} × length {100,250,500,1000}

**Dark callout band:**
On the baseline path only 1 of 8 chips was active (~87% idle), so list-price TPU and GPU land almost together: $1.25 vs $1.27 per 1k predictions. Multi-query pmap and single-query ensemble sharding (pmap + pmean) both fill the slice; after that, cost per prediction stays roughly constant as chip count grows.

**Cost per 1,000 predictions (centered trio):**
| Backend     | Cost / 1k |
|-------------|-----------|
| CPU         | $11.19    |
| GPU T4      | $1.27     |
| TPU 8-chip  | $1.25     |

## Section 8 - Reproduce (`#reproduce`)

- Kicker: Reproduce
- Headline: “Code and commands”
- Body: Docker builds for CPU/GPU and Kubernetes manifests for the class TPU cluster are in the repo.
- Link: https://github.com/lorenzopazienza/alphafold-tpu-benchmark

**Repo layout table:**
| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| configs/ | K8s Jobs (AF2 sweeps + AF3 TPU attempt) |
| figures/ | Charts + AF3 structure still |
| notebooks/ | AF2 + AF3 Google Colab notebooks |
| presentation/ | Course slides PDF |
| profiling/ | XLA trace notes |
| results/ | AF2 clocks + sweep/ + af3_comparison.md |
| src/ | AF2 spikes + make_af3_input.py |
| structure/ | Ubiquitin PDB + AF3 CIF |
| website/ | This site |

**CPU example (on page):**
```
docker build --build-arg JAX_VARIANT=cpu \
  -t af-bench:cpu .
docker run -v $(pwd)/results:/alphafold/results \
  af-bench:cpu --run_tag=cpu
```
GPU/TPU variants and Google Colab notebooks are in the README; sweep jobs under configs/.

## How to answer users about this site

1. Read this file end-to-end; treat it as the page content.
2. Separate three exhibit types:
   - **AF2 systems timing** (118-res, Haiku random init, CPU/GPU/TPU) - main study
   - **Ubiquitin ESMFold** (`#structure`) - biology demo with high mean pLDDT 90.5
   - **AF3 side-investigation** (`#af3`) - separate codebase; Google Colab Intel Xeon CPU (2 vCPU) and Google Colab NVIDIA Tesla T4 timing + interactive CIF; public AF3 has no TPU
3. Quote the tables for latency, compile ratios, costs, and experiment stats.
4. Mention amber/negative results: AF2 batching (vmap), GSPMD auto-shard, and AF3 TPU CLI gap; then the AF2 ensemble-shard fix (8/8 chips).
5. Never rank AF3 toy confidence against ubiquitin pLDDT as model quality - no-MSA input by design.
6. Link section anchors (#structure, #results, #experiments, #af3, #cost, #reproduce) or the GitHub repo for code.
